blocks.text: Walkthrough interview notes
HANGS Construction Services LLC
Fiscal year: July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026
Asked by: the audit team, August 17, 2026
Answered by: Dana Whitfield, Controller
Answered on: August 19, 2026
Status: the answers each person gave in the walkthroughs, confirmed in writing by the Controller; not a representation letter
Q1 Vendor setup, with Mei Northcott. Walk us through setting up a new vendor.

Answer: I enter the vendor from the W-9 and the Controller approves the record. When she is out I approve it myself so the job is not held up; that happened for Marten Lake Aggregates LLC, Rainier Site Supply LLC, Sound Formwork Rentals LLC. The portal lets me approve payments under $25,000.
Q2 Payment runs, with Dana Whitfield. How is a payment run approved?

Answer: Accounts Payable builds the run and I approve it in the bank portal; the Director of Operations approves anything of $100,000 or more. I did not know the portal let Accounts Payable approve small payments.
Q3 Pay applications, with Brandon Valdivia. How is a pay application prepared and approved?
Answer: I prepare it from the schedule of values and the percent complete, the owner’s architect reviews it, and the Controller approves it before it is sent. Retainage is 5% on every job.
Q4 Rate changes, with Renata Salazar. How is a pay rate changed?

Answer: From a signed personnel action form. I enter every change. My own raise was agreed in my review with the Managing Director, but I entered it before she signed the form. The payroll system can print a master file change report; we do not run it.
Q5 Payroll release, with Dana Whitfield. What do you review before releasing a payroll?
Answer: The register totals against the prior payroll, headcount and overtime. I do not see changes to rates or bank accounts unless they move the totals.
Q6 Journal entries, with Dana Whitfield. Who reviews your journal entries over $25,000?
Answer: The policy says the Director of Operations, but in practice I post my own entries at month end and nobody reviews them. I review the Project Accountant’s entries.
Q7 Bank reconciliations, with Marisol Zielinski. How is the bank reconciliation done and reviewed?
Answer: I reconcile the operating account each month within two weeks and give it to the Controller. She looks at it but has not been signing it.
Q8 User access, with Dana Whitfield. When were system permissions last reviewed?
Answer: When the bank portal was set up in 2023. I have not reviewed them since.
Demonstration document. Every name and figure is invented.

blocks.text: Process narratives FY2026
HANGS Construction Services LLC
Fiscal year: July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026
Prepared by: Dana Whitfield, Controller
Prepared on: August 3, 2026
Status: the client’s own description of its processes and key controls, for the walkthroughs
Purchasing to pay

Flow: Project managers commit job costs; vendor invoices arrive at Accounts Payable, are coded to the job and approved by the project manager, and are paid by ACH in a weekly run the Controller approves in the bank portal.
P2P-1 Vendor setup. New vendors and bank account changes are approved by the Controller in the vendor master before the first payment.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: As needed; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The vendor change log
P2P-2 Payment approval. The Controller approves every payment run in the bank portal; the preparer cannot approve; payments of $100,000 or more need the Director of Operations too.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: Weekly; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The bank portal approvals
P2P-3 Invoice approval. The project manager approves each vendor invoice against the job before it is paid.
Owner: Project managers; Frequency: Each invoice; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The approval stamp on the invoice
Billing to cash

Flow: Each month the project manager prepares the pay application from the schedule of values; the Controller approves it; the owner pays net of 5% retainage; the Project Accountant posts receipts from the bank.
B2C-1 Pay application approval. Each pay application is approved by the project manager and the Controller before it is sent.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: Monthly, each job; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The pay application log
B2C-2 Cash receipts. Receipts are posted within one business day of the deposit and agreed to the bank.
Owner: Project Accountant; Frequency: Daily; Type: Detective, manual; Evidence: The cash receipts log
Payroll
Flow: Superintendents approve crew timesheets; the Payroll and HR Manager keeps the employee master and processes payroll biweekly; the Controller approves the register before release.
PAY-1 Rate changes. A pay rate is changed only from a personnel action form signed by the approver.
Owner: Payroll and HR Manager; Frequency: As needed; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The rate change log and the forms
PAY-2 Payroll release. The Controller reviews the payroll register against the prior payroll and approves it before release.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: Biweekly; Type: Detective, manual; Evidence: The payroll approvals log
PAY-3 Leavers. A leaver is paid one final check and inactivated the same day.
Owner: Payroll and HR Manager; Frequency: As needed; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The terminations log
The close
Flow: The Controller closes each month: accruals, depreciation, the job schedule and over and under billings by manual journal entry; the Project Accountant reconciles the bank accounts.
CLS-1 Journal entry review. Manual journal entries over $25,000 are reviewed and initialed by a second person before posting.
Owner: Controller and Director of Operations; Frequency: As needed; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The journal entry listing
CLS-2 Bank reconciliation. The operating account is reconciled within 15 days of month end and reviewed, signed and dated by the Controller.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: Monthly; Type: Detective, manual; Evidence: The signed reconciliation
System access
Flow: The accounting system and the bank portal each assign permissions by user; the Controller administers both.
ITG-1 User access. The Controller assigns system roles so that no one holds two conflicting permissions.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: Annually and on change; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The user access report
Demonstration document. Every name and figure is invented.

trail.what: List the key controls in scope, set the samples and the yardstick for severity
trail.result: 11 key controls: purchasing to pay P2P-1, P2P-2, P2P-3; billing to cash B2C-1, B2C-2; payroll PAY-1, PAY-2, PAY-3; the close CLS-1, CLS-2; and user access ITG-1. The approval matrix adopted January 15, 2024 sets the terms: the preparer of a payment cannot approve it, payments of $100,000 or more need a second approval, journal entries over $25,000 need a second review, and bank reconciliations are due within 15 days. Severity is weighed against the year-end audit’s $350,000.00 materiality; the CPA decides every level.

trail.what: Walk a new vendor and its first payment through the process, end to end
trail.result: Puget Sound Shoring Co. was entered by Mei Northcott on October 20, 2025 with a W-9 and approved by Dana Whitfield the next day. Its first payment, ACH-251107-2 for $90,869.31 on November 7, 2025, was prepared by Mei Northcott, approved by Dana Whitfield in the bank portal and its invoice approved by Brandon Valdivia. P2P-1, P2P-2 and P2P-3 are designed to prevent an unauthorized vendor or payment, and are in place.

trail.what: Test every FY2026 vendor change for an approval by someone other than the person who entered it
trail.result: 9 of the 12 changes were approved by the Controller. 3 new vendors were entered by Mei Northcott and never approved: Marten Lake Aggregates LLC, Rainier Site Supply LLC, Sound Formwork Rentals LLC (P2P-1 not operating). Q1: she approves them herself when the Controller is out.

trail.what: Test every payment of $5,000 or more for who prepared and who approved it
trail.result: Of 56 payments, 52 were prepared by Accounts Payable and approved by the Controller, and all 10 of $100,000 or more have the Director of Operations’ second approval. 4, $64,675.50 in all, were prepared and approved by Mei Northcott, each under her $25,000 portal limit, and every one went to a vendor she set up without approval (P2P-2 not operating, SOD-01).

trail.what: Sample five payments of $10,000 or more with the plan’s seed and vouch each approval
trail.result: 5 payments drawn from 53: each was approved by the Controller, not its preparer, with the project manager’s approval on the invoice, and the one over $100,000 by the Director of Operations too. The sample happens to miss the 4 self-approved payments; the whole-population test found them.

trail.what: Compare the user access report with the conflicts the policy forbids
trail.result: 3 conflicts: Mei Northcott, Accounts Payable Specialist, holds both “Vendor master: add and edit” and “Bank portal: approve payments”; Mei Northcott, Accounts Payable Specialist, holds both “Bank portal: create payments” and “Bank portal: approve payments”; Renata Salazar, Payroll and HR Manager, holds both “Payroll master: edit” and “Payroll: process”. The Controller administers both systems and has not reviewed access since 2023 (Q8; ITG-1 not operating).

trail.result: 47 of the 54 manual entries are over $25,000, $9,027,953.60 in all. The 17 the Project Accountant prepared were reviewed by the Controller before posting. trail.result: All 12 were prepared by Marisol Zielinski within 15 days of month end and each reconciles to the cent. June 30: $5,554,191.74 per the bank, less 9 outstanding payments of $192,506.43, is the books’ $5,361,685.31, the trial balance’s operating cash. None of the twelve is signed as reviewed (Q7): CLS-2 is in place but its review is not evidenced (REC-01), the same gap the cash audit found in the company’s June reconciliation.

passages.q: Must HANGS Construction Services file Form 940 for 2026?
passages.a: You're subject to FUTA tax in 2026 on the wages you pay employees who aren't farmworkers or household workers if: you paid wages of $1,500 or more in any calendar quarter in 2025 or 2026, or you had one or more employees for at least some part of a day in any 20 or more different weeks in 2025 or 20 or more different weeks in 2026.

passages.q: What are the 2026 FUTA rate, wage base and credit?
passages.a: For 2026, the FUTA tax rate is 6.0%. The tax applies to the first $7,000 you pay to each employee as wages during the year. ... The credit may be as much as 5.4% of FUTA taxable wages. If you're entitled to the maximum 5.4% credit, the FUTA tax rate after credit is 0.6%.

passages.q: Do employees' 401(k) deferrals come off FUTA wages?
passages.a: Elective employee contributions and deferrals to a plan containing a qualified cash or deferred compensation arrangement (401(k)). Generally exempt, but see section 402(g) for limitation. Taxable. Taxable.

passages.q: When is the Q3 2026 Form 941 due?
passages.a: Your Form 941 is due by the last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter. ... 3. July, August, September September 30 October 31 ... If you made timely deposits in full payment of your taxes for the quarter, you may file by the 10th day of the 2nd month that follows the end of the quarter. ... If any due date for filing falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, you may file your return on the next business day.

passages.q: Which employees are counted on line 1, and what goes on lines 2 and 3?
passages.a: Enter the number of employees on your payroll for the pay period including March 12, June 12, September 12, or December 12, for the quarter indicated at the top of Form 941. ... Enter amounts on line 2 that would also be included in box 1 of your employees’ Forms W-2. ... Enter the federal income tax you withheld (or were required to withhold) from your employees on this quarter’s wages, tips, taxable fringe benefits, and supplemental unemployment compensation benefits.

passages.q: Which wages go on line 5a, and where does Social Security stop for each employee?
passages.a: The social security tax rate is 6.2% each for the employee and employer. The social security wage base limit is $184,500. ... For 2026, the rate of social security tax on taxable wages is 6.2% (0.062) each for the employer and employee. Stop paying social security tax on and entering an employee’s wages on line 5a when the employee’s taxable wages and tips reach $184,500 for the year. ... line 5a (column 1) x 0.124 line 5a (column 2)

sources.title: General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 (2026)

passages.q: When are the 2026 Forms W-2 and W-3 due, and must they be e-filed?
passages.a: The due date for filing 2026 Forms W-2 ... and W-3 ... with the SSA is February 1, 2027, whether you file using paper forms or electronically. ... Generally, you must furnish Copies B, C, and 2 of Form W-2 to your employees by February 1, 2027. ... You must e-file Forms W-2 ... if you are required to file at least 10 information returns.

passages.q: What goes in box 1, and are the 401(k) deferrals and Washington Paid Leave premiums in it?
passages.a: Box 1-Wages, tips, other compensation. Show the total taxable wages, tips, and other compensation that you paid to your employee during the year. However, do not include elective deferrals (such as employee contributions to a section 401(k) or 403(b) plan) ... You must include the employee contribution and the employer voluntary payment as wages on the Form W-2.

passages.q: What are the 2026 Social Security limits for boxes 3 and 4, and what goes in boxes 5 and 6?
passages.a: The total of boxes 3 and 7 cannot exceed $184,500 (2026 maximum social security wage base). ... For 2026, the amount should not exceed $11,439 ... there is no wage base limit for Medicare tax ... an employer is required to withhold a 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on any Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) wages ... in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year.

checks.title: SOD-01
checks.detail: Significant deficiency, proposed (P2P-1, P2P-2, ITG-1). Mei Northcott, Accounts Payable Specialist, can set up vendors and approve payments. She set up Marten Lake Aggregates LLC, Rainier Site Supply LLC, Sound Formwork Rentals LLC without approval and approved 4 payments to them herself, $64,675.50, each under her portal limit. The invoices are for job materials and nothing suggests the vendors are not real, but the controls that would stop a fictitious vendor were bypassed. Recommendation: remove her approval permission in the bank portal; have the Controller approve every vendor setup and bank change before payment; review the vendor change report monthly; confirm the three vendors’ bank details by calling a number on file; review system access every year.

checks.title: JE-01
checks.detail: Significant deficiency, proposed (CLS-1). 30 manual entries over $25,000, $8,045,083.44, were prepared and posted by the Controller with no second review, including accruals, depreciation and the over and under billings. The quarterly review later found September interest was never accrued (INT-01), the kind of error a second review catches. Recommendation: the Director of Operations reviews and initials the Controller’s entries over the threshold before posting, turn on the system’s approval step, and sign a monthly close checklist. The CPA considers whether this and SOD-01 together are a material weakness.

checks.title: PAY-01
checks.detail: Deficiency, proposed (PAY-1, PAY-2). Renata Salazar, Payroll and HR Manager, can edit the payroll master and process payroll; she entered her own raise, $88,000.00 to $98,000.00, before the form was signed, and $4,999.93 more was paid to June 30 (the payroll audit’s RATE-01). The Controller’s review sees totals only, and the master file change report is never run. Recommendation: run the change report every payroll and have the Controller review and sign it; the Managing Director signs PAF-25-119 or the pay is corrected.

checks.title: REC-01
checks.detail: Deficiency, proposed (CLS-2). All 12 operating account reconciliations were prepared on time and reconcile, and June ties to the trial balance, but none is signed as reviewed. The cash audit found the same in the company’s June reconciliation. Recommendation: the Controller signs and dates each reconciliation within the 15 days and follows up any item older than 60 days.

checks.title: SCOPE-01
checks.detail: Walkthroughs of eleven key controls with small samples, for the lender and the board. Not an examination of internal control and no opinion on it; controls not listed in the narratives were not tested.

checks.title: RESP-01
checks.detail: Management’s responses to SOD-01, JE-01, PAY-01 and REC-01, with owners and dates, have not been obtained. The CPA requests them before anything goes to Cinderbrook Bank or the board.

checks.title: SIGN-01
checks.detail: These are draft workpapers and findings for the engagement shareholder. They give no opinion on internal control. Nothing has been signed, posted or sent to the client, the bank or the board.

checks.title: Purchasing · Payments Approved by Their Preparer (SOD-01)
Close · Manual Entries Over the Threshold
Close · June Reconciliation Less the Trial Balance
List the key controls in scope, set the samples and the yardstick for severity
checks.detail: 11 key controls: purchasing to pay P2P-1, P2P-2, P2P-3; billing to cash B2C-1, B2C-2; payroll PAY-1, PAY-2, PAY-3; the close CLS-1, CLS-2; and user access ITG-1. The approval matrix adopted January 15, 2024 sets the terms: the preparer of a payment cannot approve it, payments of $100,000 or more need a second approval, journal entries over $25,000 need a second review, and bank reconciliations are due within 15 days. Severity is weighed against the year-end audit’s $350,000.00 materiality; the CPA decides every level.

checks.title: Walk a new vendor and its first payment through the process, end to end
checks.detail: Puget Sound Shoring Co. was entered by Mei Northcott on October 20, 2025 with a W-9 and approved by Dana Whitfield the next day. Its first payment, ACH-251107-2 for $90,869.31 on November 7, 2025, was prepared by Mei Northcott, approved by Dana Whitfield in the bank portal and its invoice approved by Brandon Valdivia. P2P-1, P2P-2 and P2P-3 are designed to prevent an unauthorized vendor or payment, and are in place.

checks.title: Test every FY2026 vendor change for an approval by someone other than the person who entered it
checks.detail: 9 of the 12 changes were approved by the Controller. 3 new vendors were entered by Mei Northcott and never approved: Marten Lake Aggregates LLC, Rainier Site Supply LLC, Sound Formwork Rentals LLC (P2P-1 not operating). Q1: she approves them herself when the Controller is out.

checks.title: Test every payment of $5,000 or more for who prepared and who approved it
checks.detail: Of 56 payments, 52 were prepared by Accounts Payable and approved by the Controller, and all 10 of $100,000 or more have the Director of Operations’ second approval. 4, $64,675.50 in all, were prepared and approved by Mei Northcott, each under her $25,000 portal limit, and every one went to a vendor she set up without approval (P2P-2 not operating, SOD-01).

checks.title: Sample five payments of $10,000 or more with the plan’s seed and vouch each approval
checks.detail: 5 payments drawn from 53: each was approved by the Controller, not its preparer, with the project manager’s approval on the invoice, and the one over $100,000 by the Director of Operations too. The sample happens to miss the 4 self-approved payments; the whole-population test found them.

checks.title: Compare the user access report with the conflicts the policy forbids
checks.detail: 3 conflicts: Mei Northcott, Accounts Payable Specialist, holds both “Vendor master: add and edit” and “Bank portal: approve payments”; Mei Northcott, Accounts Payable Specialist, holds both “Bank portal: create payments” and “Bank portal: approve payments”; Renata Salazar, Payroll and HR Manager, holds both “Payroll master: edit” and “Payroll: process”. The Controller administers both systems and has not reviewed access since 2023 (Q8; ITG-1 not operating).

checks.title: Walk a pay application from approval to the cash received
checks.detail: J-2604-2512, $2,231,620.00 for Pier Nine Commercial LLC, was approved by Brandon Valdivia on January 3, 2026 and by the Controller on January 4, 2026, sent as HGC-25-1021 on January 5, 2026, and paid net of 5% retainage, $2,120,039.00, on February 16, 2026; it was posted on February 17, 2026. B2C-1 and B2C-2 are in place.

checks.title: Sample five pay applications and test the approvals and the retainage
checks.detail: All 5 were approved by the project manager and then the Controller before they were sent, and each one’s 5% retainage and net due recompute. B2C-1 operates.

checks.title: Sample five receipts and test that each was posted within a business day and agrees to its invoice
checks.detail: All 5 were posted within one business day of the deposit, for exactly the invoice’s net due. B2C-2 operates.

checks.title: Walk a payroll from processing to release
checks.detail: PR-26-06, paid March 20, 2026: processed by Renata Salazar, the register ($456,522.27 gross for 96 people) reviewed by Dana Whitfield on March 18, 2026 and released on March 19, 2026. The master file change report was “not run”: the review sees totals, not the rate and bank account changes behind them (Q5). PAY-2 is in place but not designed to catch a master file change.

checks.title: Sample three payrolls and test that each was reviewed before it was released
checks.detail: All 3 were reviewed by the Controller before release, by someone other than the person who processed them. The master file change report was never run in any of the 27 payrolls.

checks.title: Vouch every rate change to a signed form, and every leaver to a final check
checks.detail: 4 of 5 rate changes have a form signed before entry. The fifth is Renata Salazar’s own salary, $88,000.00 to $98,000.00: she entered it, the form is unsigned (Q4) and she can both edit the master file and process payroll. 13 paychecks at the new rate paid $4,999.93 more (the payroll audit’s RATE-01). PAY-1 does not operate for her own pay (PAY-01). All 6 leavers were paid one final check and inactivated that day: PAY-3 operates.

checks.title: Test every manual journal entry over $25,000 for a second person’s review before posting
checks.detail: 47 of the 54 manual entries are over $25,000, $9,027,953.60 in all. The 17 the Project Accountant prepared were reviewed by the Controller before posting. The 30 the Controller prepared, $8,045,083.44, were posted by her with no second review, among them AJ-25-1205 (Over and under billings, December 2025, $1,119,919.00), AJ-26-0605 (Over and under billings, June 2026, $979,098.00), AJ-25-0905 (Over and under billings, September 2025, $928,912.00). The Director of Operations holds the approval permission and has never used it (Q6). CLS-1 does not operate (JE-01).

checks.title: Test all twelve bank reconciliations for timeliness, arithmetic and the Controller’s review, and tie June 30 to the trial balance
checks.detail: All 12 were prepared by Marisol Zielinski within 15 days of month end and each reconciles to the cent. June 30: $5,554,191.74 per the bank, less 9 outstanding payments of $192,506.43, is the books’ $5,361,685.31, the trial balance’s operating cash. None of the twelve is signed as reviewed (Q7): CLS-2 is in place but its review is not evidenced (REC-01), the same gap the cash audit found in the company’s June reconciliation.
